item.title: The Robot Report parent Arrowfly launches AI for Engineers platform, events for engineers navigating AI
item.dc:creator: The Robot Report Staff
item.description:
The initiative for engineers includes a news desk, a conference, research, and an advisory board, grounded in trusted editorial brands.

The post The Robot Report parent Arrowfly launches AI for Engineers platform, events for engineers navigating AI appeared first on The Robot Report.
item.ns3:encoded:
Arrowfly has launched AI for Engineers, a resource including news, events, and an advisory board. Source: Arrowfly

Arrowfly, the parent company of The Robot Report, today launched AI for Engineers, a resource for engineers and technical leaders applying artificial intelligence in their work. Anchored by Arrowfly’s network of more than 20 engineering brands, collectively reaching 2.1 million verified industry readers, 29 million website visitors, 1.6 million email subscribers, and generating 202 million monthly impressions, AI for Engineers brings together four interconnected pillars: a dedicated News Desk, a flagship annual conference, original research, and an Advisory Board. Together, they form a platform providing practical knowledge, peer connections, and professional guidance as AI reshapes the engineering profession.

The demand is already there. More than 30,000 engineering and technical professionals have engaged with AI topics across Arrowfly’s engineering portfolio through webinars, newsletters, and editorial content. Organizations are now investing in AI across every core function, from research and development and design to automation, manufacturing operations, cybersecurity, and workforce development.

As AI adoption accelerates, the need for practical, hands-on knowledge is becoming increasingly important. AI for Engineers was built to meet that demand: a year-round destination combining rigorous editorial coverage, peer-driven applied learning, and an advisory structure accountable to practitioners.

“AI is no longer a future-state consideration for engineers. It is a present-tense operational reality across product design, manufacturing, robotics, medtech, and energy,” stated Amanda Buehner, senior vice president, sales & strategy, engineering, Arrowfly.

“What we’re hearing from engineering leaders is that the challenge isn’t whether to adopt AI. It’s how to move from experimentation to practical, repeatable applications that deliver results,” she added. “AI for Engineers is built around that need, bringing the industry together around trusted information, real-world implementation, and direct exchange between practitioners.”

Four pillars, one mission for engineers

News desk: The AI for Engineers News Desk puts specialized editors inside each engineering discipline to report on how AI is changing the work: the tools practitioners are adopting, the workflows being rebuilt, and the decisions technologists are navigating right now. Backed by more than 20 engineering brands, it is the only editorial resource built from the ground up for engineers who are already building with AI.

Live event: AI for Engineers will take place Sept. 20 to 22, 2027, at M Resort Spa Casino in Henderson, Nev., just outside Las Vegas. The three-day conference will bring together an expected 700 engineers and technical leaders to learn how AI is being designed, built, and deployed across the product and plant lifecycle.

Engineers who attend face a shared pressure: Leadership has committed to AI, budgets are moving, and the question is how to build something that works. The program will span five discipline-specific content tracks covering Engineering Design and Automation, Medical Devices and Medtech, Robotics, Energy and Electronics, and Industrial Operations and Smart Manufacturing. They will draw mechanical engineers, design engineers, CAD/CAE specialists, product development managers, R&D directors, medical device engineers, regulatory affairs professionals, clinical engineers, biomedical researchers, robotics and automation engineers, warehouse operations managers, systems integrators, manufacturing executives, and electrical engineers.

The format combines daily keynotes, editorial sessions, pre-scheduled 1:1 meetings, and speaking slots, with Day 3 closing in peer-to-peer guided conversations structured around specific AI topics. A welcome reception on Day 1 and an offsite dinner on Day 2 round out the program. Attendees will leave with practical, vendor-tested AI workflows they can apply immediately.

Engineers and technical leaders can register now for AI for Engineers 2027.

Original research: The AI for Engineers research program launches the 2027 Outlook of AI, an original peer-to-peer study spanning five disciplines: AI in Engineering Design and Simulation, AI in Medical Devices and Medtech, AI in Robotics and Automation, AI in Energy and Electronics, and AI in Industrial Operations and Smart Manufacturing.

The study intends to capture how organizations are adopting AI by function, what is working, where the barriers remain, and what leaders expect by 2030. Results will be compiled into a gated report published in Q4 2026 and distributed across Arrowfly’s engineering portfolio and beyond. Engineers who complete the survey and qualify receive a complimentary pass to AI for Engineers 2027.

Advisory board: Completing the initiative is the AI for Engineers Advisory Board, a council of engineering and technical leaders shaping the standards, ethics, and best practices of AI in engineering. The Advisory Board holds the entire program accountable to the professionals it serves, ensuring that editorial coverage, conference programming, and research priorities reflect real practitioner priorities, not vendor agendas.

Solution providers and technology companies can reach AI for Engineers’ audience of 2.1 million verified professionals, spanning every discipline from mechanical and design to robotics, Medtech, energy, and industrial operations, at organizations including Amazon, NVIDIA, Boeing, Siemens, Medtronic, and Tesla. To learn about sponsorship and partnership opportunities, contact Arrowfly’s Engineering team.

About Arrowfly

Cleveland-based Arrowfly is a live and digital business-to-business destination serving professionals across the engineering, healthcare, food, retail, and hospitality sectors. Across over 40 brands, the award-winning company delivers trusted journalism, original content, live and digital events, video, and demand generation programs to the decision-makers shaping their industries.

Arrowfly produces The Robot Report, RoboBusiness, Automated Warehouse, and the Robotics Summit & Expo, among many other online brands and events.

Powered by Clara, Arrowfly’s proprietary performance platform, partners can get real-time visibility into audience engagement, lead quality, and campaign ROI. The media and marketing company is backed by an established reputation for editorial independence and credibility across the markets it serves.
